hook: Chile is 4,270 km long and on average only 177 km wide.
twist: The Andes fixed the east side (an 1881 treaty put the border on the highest peaks that divide the waters), the Pacific the west. The north came from a war over fertilizer: Chile took Bolivia's coast, and Bolivia, landlocked since, still keeps a navy on Lake Titicaca and a Day of the Sea.
angle: A shape question with a war-and-navy payoff. 3D flight down the whole country; paper soldiers, a nitrate sack and a tiny navy on a lake.
why_now: Evergreen; scout: why-Chile-is-so-long Shorts top 31.9M, median of top 25 0.34M since mid-2024; the Bolivian-navy payoff is less used.
risks: Length figures differ (4,270 km in Geography of Chile, 'over 4,300' in Chile): use 4,270 and its 177 km average.
Do not say Bolivia's navy only sails the lake: it also patrols rivers.
